story.title: Liam and Emma's Visit to the Wildlife Reserve

paragraphs.text: Last Saturday morning, Liam and his sister Emma visited the Green Valley Nature Reserve with their school science club. The reserve was divided into four main sections to represent different world habitats. Their guide was Ranger David, who had worked with wild animals for more than ten years. He gave each child a map and a notebook to write down observations.

First, the group entered the desert exhibit. The ground was covered with orange sand and large flat stones. Emma noticed a desert tortoise moving slowly toward a hole in the ground. Ranger David explained that tortoises dig deep burrows to escape the scorching heat of the afternoon sun. Liam took a photo and wrote in his notebook that the burrow keeps the animal cool and safe.

Next, they walked through the double doors into the tropical rainforest zone. Tall palm trees reached up toward the glass dome, and colorful orchids hung from branches. Suddenly, Emma heard high-pitched whistling from the treetops. Looking through his binoculars, Liam spotted two scarlet parrots perching high in the leafy canopy. At the end of the day, Ranger David thanked the children and told them that protecting natural habitats is the most important duty of all wildlife scientists.
